explanation: Rough Guides describes intimate public behavior like kissing and cuddling in Egypt as a clear no-no, with even hand-holding between an opposite-gender couple drawing disapproval in most settings. Cultural Atlas notes the norm is primarily social rather than a strict legal one: close friends of the same gender may hold hands or kiss cheeks in public without issue, while mixed-gender affection is the behavior to avoid.
local_tip: Stick to a handshake or verbal greeting in public, and save affection for private settings.
regional_note: Cairo and Alexandria's more secular social circles tend to be somewhat more tolerant of mild PDA than rural areas and Upper Egypt.

also_check.note: Public affection carries real legal risk, with past cases resulting in arrest and jail time for kissing in public.
Cheek-kissing as a greeting and casual public affection are widely accepted.
Public affection is uncommon and can draw uncomfortable looks even among young couples.
